medSchoolStudLife.diversity: For over 130 years, Meharry has produced a large percentage of the underrepresented health professionals in the United States and abroad.
medSchoolStudLife.leaveOfAbsence:
A leave of absence is an interruption of the normal course of  study requested by the student which requires prior written approval by the Dean or his/her designee. A student's leave of absence shall not extend beyond one calendar year. The official date of leave shall not antedate the date of the student's request. An official leave of absence form must be processed and can be obtained from the Office of Student and Academic Affairs.

A leave of absence may be granted upon receipt of a written request for reasons of illness, personal and/or family exigencies, financial straits, emotional states and other similar type situations. The Associate Dean for Student and Academic Affairs may require documentation to accompany a request. If the situation is appropriate, the Associate Dean for Student and Academic Affairs may place a student on an Administrative Leave of Absence. medSchoolStudLife.organizationActivities:
Student organizations are plentiful at Meharry.  Students can choose from more than 50 approved student organizations.  The student government organization at Meharry is the Pre-Alumni Association.   There are also many professional groups such as the Student National Medical Association and the American Medical Student Association.   

Community involvement could have no better exemplification than Meharry's annual Community Day.  This day allows students from all schools of the College to come together to provide educational and fun activities for the children and their parents of our urban community. In addition, students hold numerous fundraisers and clothing/food drives throughout the year to donate to shelters and community food banks.  Intramural Sports are also a part of student life at Meharry including softball and basketball.
medSchoolStudLife.setting: Meharry is located in Nashville, TN centrally located near the vibrant downtown community. Nashville has two nicknames: “Music City USA,” for the city’s musical heritage, and “Athens of the South,” for the city’s dedication to fine arts and numerous colleges and universities. Its campus in north Nashville places Meharry at the epicenter of Middle Tennessee's most vulnerable citizens. As such, Meharry students, faculty, staff, and residents provide services where they are most needed.
medSchoolStudLife.housing: On campus there are the Royal Towers, a 10-story residential complex which contains 156 apartments, Dorothy Brown Hall, which houses 70 students and Morena Place A and B which contains 100 Apartments. Meharry Medical College Living-Learning Center is located on the corner of 21st Avenue North on the southwest side of Campus. The building is a six-story structure consisting of a single-level parking garage, 126 apartment-style units, flexible teaching spaces and retail spaces. The facility also houses offices, support, resident amenities and outdoor terraces. The college also maintains a list of available off-campus accommodations in the Nashville area.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystems: The organizations and support systems on campus are as diverse as our student body. For more information on specific support and activities for gender and sexual minority students in the School of Medicine, please contact Ms. Sonya Smith, Director of Student Life at ssmith@mmc.edu.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystemsForDisabilities: Meharry Medical College is committed to the provisions of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973 and Americans with Disabilities Act in creating an inclusive community for students with disabilities. Students seeking accommodations for any type of disability are encouraged to contact the ADA Coordinator. Services include, but are not limited to, extended time for testing, assistance with locating sign language interpreters, audiotaped textbooks, physical adaptations, note-takers and reading services. Accommodations are tailored to meet the needs of each student with a documented disability. Specific concerns pertaining to services for people with disabilities or any disability issue should be directed to the ADA Coordinator.
medSchoolStudLife.wellnessPrograms:
Meharry Medical College Counseling Services, which operates as a unit of the Division of Student Affairs, was established to assist students with the balance of professional studies and personal issues. The Counseling Services is located on Meharry campus in the Cal Turner Family Center for Student Education, third floor. Counseling for students and their significant others is provided by Professional Health Service Providers who have no teaching or evaluative role with the students.

Meharry Connect offers a place for students to talk about concerns during free, confidential 15-minute consultations. You can have someone listen to you and offer support, or you might prefer to receive expert suggestions about solutions and resources. This service is available to enrolled Meharry Medical College students via HIPAA-compliant Zoom.

Therapy Assistance Online (TAO) includes over 150 brief, effective, educational sessions covering over 50 common topics and skills related to mental health, wellness, and substance use issues. TAO Includes interactive sessions, mindfulness exercises and practice tools all aimed at helping you achieve your goals.

WellConnect offers programs specifically designed to help students manage and improve their mental health as they work to achieve their goals. WellConnect gives Meharry the opportunity to take care of its students – the right way.

Wellness Workshops are led by Meharry Counseling Staff and open to Meharry Students, every Tuesday, 12pm-1pm. No prior registration required.
medSchoolStudLife.campusCulture: Located near Nashville’s historic Jefferson Street, nestled between two neighboring historically black universities, and near Nashville’s thriving downtown, Meharry provides students with a full range of auxiliary services to make their experience on campus both intellectually stimulating, socially comfortable and enjoyable.

medSchoolCurriculum.tutoringPrograms: To help bridge the gap between classroom teaching & individual studying, tutoring services are available through the Anna Cherrie Epps, Ph.D. Center for Academic Success and Achievement (CASA).
medSchoolCurriculum.curricularHighlights: The School of Medicine at Meharry Medical College has an integrated curriculum during the first-year in which instruction is organized into modules that include basic, clinical, and social sciences. The modules include Principles and Practice of Medicine, Molecular Cell Biology, Genetics, Gross Anatomy, and Embryology; also included are Integrated Neuroscience, Immunology, Principles of Infectious Disease, and Foundations in Human Disease and Treatment. The second-year is organized around a series of organ systems. The clinical years consist of the following blocks: family medicine, psychiatry, obstetrics and gynecology, pediatrics, internal medicine, surgery, an ambulatory rotation served in an urban or rural underserved area, internal medicine subinternship, capstone, and radiology, as well as guided electives.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchPrograms:
Center for Women's Health Research-addressing diseases unique to women, particularly those experienced at higher rates among minority populations. Current & future research studies at the CWHR are in the areas of reproductive health, cardiovascular disease, HIV/AIDS, breast cancer, & social & environmental factors in women's health, as well as health care access & quality. 

Center for AIDS Health Disparities Research-unraveling the biology of HIV/AIDS & seeking remedies for the populations most affected. The CAHDR has three major areas of focus: biology, behavioral, & community outreach. 

The Clinical & Translational Research Center is a training infrastructure that serves as an incubator for Meharry scientists who pursue translational research. The purpose of the CTRC is to provide the resources necessary to facilitate translational, community-based, & multi-center clinical research projects at Meharry
medSchoolCurriculum.communityServiceText: Meharry's reach extends to the community through a variety of programs that assist underserved populations.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchThesisText: Encouraged in areas of health disparities.
medSchoolCurriculum.affiliatedHospitals: Affiliated Hospitals are Metropolitan General Hospital, Blanchfield Army Hospital, Veterans Affairs, Tennessee Valley Health Care System, Southern Hills Medical Center, and Vanderbilt Health.

medSchoolInformation.generalInformation: In 1876, Meharry Medical College was founded and established as the Meharry Medical Department of Central Tennessee College by the Freedmen's Aid Society of the Methodist Episcopal Church. Meharry's inception was part of the society's continuing effort to educate freed slaves and to provide health care services for the poor and underserved. Today, the School of Medicine continues to provide excellent educational opportunities to promising students from groups underrepresented in medicine. Clinical teaching facilities include the Metropolitan Nashville General Hospital; Blanchfield Army Hospital; Veterans Affairs Tennessee Valley Health Care System, Nashville Campus and the Alvin C. York Murfreesboro Campus; Vanderbilt's Monroe Carrell Children's Hospital; and a number of affiliated hospitals and clinics. The provision of primary care, particularly in medically underserved areas, is a special emphasis, as is health disparities research.
medSchoolInformation.missionStatement: Meharry Medical College is a global academic health sciences center advancing health equity through innovative research, transformative education, exceptional and compassionate health services, and policy-influencing thought leadership. True to its legacy, Meharry empowers diverse populations to improve the well-being of humankind.  The School of Medicine is dedicated to the educational, intellectual, professional, and personal development of a diverse group of exceptional students, faculty, residents, and staff who are deeply committed to the study and practice of medicine.  These are our core values: accountability with transparency; equity with inclusion; respect with collegiality; service with compassion; and integrity without exception.

For applicants that are submitting coursework completed at a community college, the coursework will be considered if it meets the following criteria:
Coursework was delivered and completed in an “in-person” format.
Coursework was completed at a regionally accredited institution.
Coursework demonstrates a level of academic rigor appropriate for students looking to complete advanced study in the sciences.
medSchoolApplication.letterOfIntentAdditionalInfo: The Admissions Committee of Meharry Medical College will review no more than 2 Notices of Significant Updates per applicant per cycle.  These updates should be submitted in PDF-format to admissions@mmc.edu prior to receiving a final determination.
medSchoolApplication.technicalStandardInfo: Medical education requires that the accumulation of scientific knowledge be accompanied by the simultaneous acquisition of skills, professional attitudes and behavior. All courses in the curriculum are required in order to develop essential skills critical to becoming a competent physician. Graduates of medical schools must have the knowledge and skills to function in a broad variety of clinical situations and to render a wide spectrum of patient care. Meharry Medical College, School of Medicine acknowledges Section 504 of the 1973 Vocational Rehabilitation Act, PL 101-336 - the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) 1993, and the ADA Amendments Act of 2008 - PL 110-325 but ascertains that certain minimum technical standards must be present in prospective candidates. A candidate for the M.D. degree must have aptitude, abilities and skills in five areas: (1) observation (2) communication (3) motor function (4) quantitative and intellectual conception (5) behavioral and social stability.

medSchoolFinancial.financialAid: Financial aid awards are based on analyses of student needs & academic achievement. The limited financial aid program includes scholarships, grants, work study, & loans. Because of fluctuations in federal & private support for financial aid programs, the types & amounts of awards are revised & adjusted on a continuing basis. Therefore, it is necessary that applicants plan their financial program as carefully as their academic program.

medSchoolPrograms.info: The Meharry Cancer Summer Research Program (SuRP) is an intensive, hands-on research experience for undergraduate and medical students. The overall goals of the program are to expose students to different types of cancer research (basic, translational, clinical, community-based, and bioinformatics-based) and increase their awareness of cancer health disparities. Program participants will work under the mentorship of a Meharry Medical College and/or Vanderbilt University Medical Center faculty on a research project that explores the causes, diagnosis, prevention and/or treatment of cancer.

medSchoolSelection.selectionFactors: Applicants are selected based on a holistic review of both cognitive and non-cognitive skills that denote probable success in medical school. These factors include but are not limited to academic performance in the basic science prerequisites, MCAT scores, letters of recommendation, personal statement, and strength of experiences. Interviews are by invitation only.  Meharry Medical College seeks to attract a wide demographic, cultural and educational population to reflect the caliber of social interchange in which the eventual practice of medicine will occur. Meharry Medical Colleg does not discriminate on the basis of gender, sexual orientation, race, age, religion, color, national origin, handicap, veteran, immigrant status
